body.x: Otiton Medical Co., Ltd. (CEO Jaeyoung Jayden Kim) announced that it participated in the “Global Media Meetup” hosted by AVING News’ International Press Club (IPC) for domestic companies and startups on Friday, December 12, at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul.

The Global Media Meetup focuses on introducing Korean companies’ and startups’ products and technologies to the global market. In particular, it aims to proactively report on CES 2026 Innovation Award winners and CES-participating startups through global media channels and expand business opportunities.

Founded in 2022, Otiton Medical is a healthcare technology company led by CEO Jaeyoung Kim, who majored in electronic engineering and brings more than 17 years of hardware design experience. He directly contributes to the development of smart thermometers and therapeutic devices, as well as to overall technical planning. Notably, the company enables users to effectively check and manage ear-related conditions at home, a process that previously required hospital visits.

The company’s flagship brand, Doctor In Home, provides personalized health management and AI-assisted diagnostic functions through AI- and IoT-based smart medical devices. Users can easily check their health status at home and conduct more systematic monitoring based on accumulated data.

Since October 2024, Otiton Medical has officially introduced its first product, a smart thermometer, at major global exhibitions, including MWC Las Vegas, BIO Japan, HLTH Las Vegas, AusBio Australia, and MWC Barcelona. At CES 2025, the product won an Innovation Award in the Mobile Devices and Apps category, proving both its technological strength and market potential.

In Korea, the company participated in exhibitions such as GMEP and NEXTRISE, creating contact points with numerous overseas buyers, and it currently continues active partnership discussions with companies in Türkiye and Singapore.

body.cap: Smart therapeutic device | Image provided by Otiton Medical

body.x: Otiton Medical will showcase a smart device at CES 2026 that combines precision medical technology with AI. The smart therapeutic device for humans integrates an endoscopic camera and an infrared sensor from the existing smart thermometer, allowing users to check inflammation and wounds inside the ear in real time and support infrared-based treatment.

The smart thermometer for companion animals incorporates animal-specific clinical algorithms and a high-sensitivity temperature sensor to measure changes in body temperature precisely. Unlike humans, animals have an eardrum structure that is closer to a right angle, requiring the camera to be inserted more deeply. Veterinarians traditionally measure body temperature rectally. For this reason, the device uses a non-contact infrared sensor to measure temperature in the hip area.

Ahead of the opening of CES 2026, Otiton Medical achieved the milestone of winning an Innovation Award in the “Mobile Devices, Accessories & Apps” category with this product, marking its second consecutive year receiving a CES Innovation Award.
In addition, the smart therapeutic device for companion animals visualizes abnormal areas with an endoscopic camera and provides infrared heat therapy.

According to the company, all of these products feature curved form factors and soft color tones designed with intuitiveness and portability in mind. At the same time, the animal devices use skin-friendly materials and noise-minimizing designs to reduce stress. The user interface employs one-button operation and LCD feedback to make it easy for elderly users and first-time users to operate the devices.

body.cap: Smart thermometer and smart therapeutic device for companion animals | Image provided by Otiton Medical

body.x: A key innovation of the three products to be introduced at this CES is compressing high-specification equipment previously used only in hospitals into consumer-friendly, home-use devices. By integrating endoscopy and heat therapy into a single device and linking it to a smartphone-based cloud-monitoring system, the company offers a level of functionality that remains rare even in the companion animal healthcare market.

Their “global problem-solving capability” also stands out. Otiton Medical’s solutions allow users to check their health at home and safely perform early treatment with a 650nm infrared lamp. They also help narrow gaps in companion animal medical services, offering responses to global issues such as limited medical infrastructure, aging societies, and the growing pet family population.

The smart thermometer, which won a CES Innovation Award in 2025, features an endoscopic camera and high-precision sensors, enabling early diagnosis of ear diseases such as otitis media at home. AI-based analysis and mobile app integration further improve usability and accuracy.

Following this recognition, Otiton Medical saw a sharp rise in brand awareness across global markets, including the United States, Japan, China, Australia, and Vietnam, and received partnership proposals from overseas hospitals and distributors. The company explained that the award also expanded business opportunities, including invitations to domestic and international exhibitions, discussions with large corporations, and investment attraction, serving as an essential turning point in building a foundation for the global expansion of the Doctor In Home platform.

Otiton Medical is currently establishing customized strategies tailored to medical regulations and distribution structures in each country. It plans to spread technology-driven health management solutions worldwide through collaboration with global partners.

To expand AI technology–based health management solutions globally, starting in Korea and Japan, Otiton Medical plans to continue participating in major global exhibitions, such as CES 2026, showcase its smart healthcare technologies, and expand distribution partnerships in key target countries, including the United States, Australia, and Singapore.

body.x: Meanwhile, AVING News has introduced Korean companies to the world through partnership cooperation with more than 800 media outlets across 54 countries over the past 22 years. Building on its long-established global media network, AVING News launched the International Press Club in August. Media outlets participating in this Global Media Meetup included Innovation & Tech Today from the United States, Le Café Du Geek from France, Arageek from the United Arab Emirates, and Digitimes from Taiwan.
